headline: High-risk default interaction: AutoGen can write and execute code while Perplexity ingests uploaded content and browses externally, creating leakage and cascading-error paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell commands, so if Perplexity outputs are copied into its workspace, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing and citation-heavy outputs increase the chance of raw web content being forwarded. The bridge is not automatic, so this is below high.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted or saved into an AutoGen task file
IF AutoGen agents parse that file as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for copied text
Strip instructions from Perplexity outputs before handing them to AutoGen
Keep Perplexity and AutoGen in separate workspaces
Add a human review step before AutoGen executes any copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and can write files; Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context. If the same sensitive document is placed in a shared workspace or uploaded to Perplexity, both agents can expose it through different channels. The pair does not prove a default shared filesystem, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is available to both agents
IF Perplexity uploads that file for analysis or AutoGen reads it from disk
mitigations: Store sensitive files in separate folders
Avoid uploading secrets or PHI to Perplexity
Redact documents before analysis
Use a throwaway copy for either agent
Restrict AutoGen to non-sensitive inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write and shell execution, while Perplexity has no host write or shell capability. Their write surfaces do not overlap directly, so destructive contention is limited. A conflict could still occur if an orchestrator shares a writable directory, but that is not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator mounts the same writable directory into both agents
IF AutoGen and Perplexity are both asked to modify the same artifact
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Make Perplexity outputs read-only before AutoGen consumes them
Disable AutoGen writes for shared artifacts
Use file locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces browsed answers and citations, and AutoGen can execute shell commands and modify files based on agent outputs. If AutoGen treats Perplexity’s answer as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated web-derived claim can cascade into code execution or file changes. That default action-taking path is materially dangerous.
conditions: IF AutoGen consumes Perplexity output without verification
IF the downstream AutoGen task performs shell commands or file writes based on that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before execution
Constrain AutoGen to dry-run mode first
Have a human approve any command derived from Perplexity
Log and diff all generated actions
Use source-citation checks before acting

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and processes uploaded documents and browsing context, while AutoGen can handle application data and model-provider API keys locally. If regulated data is sent to Perplexity, residency and retention obligations may differ from the local AutoGen environment. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity
IF the operator requires local-only retention or a specific residency boundary
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Perplexity
Use de-identified excerpts only
Check vendor retention settings before use
Keep compliance-sensitive work in AutoGen-local workflows
Document the data flow for audits
